To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

myocardial stiffness derived from the end-systole relation between wall stress and the logarithm of the inverse of wall thickness is independent of ventricle size and is sensitive in detecting changes in contractility.
kSM, a contractile index independent of ventricle size, is sensitive to changes of inotropic state.

the stiffness constant of myocardium (k), derived from the end-systole pressure-wall thickness relation, is independent of ventricle size and is sensitive and specific for changes in myocardial contractility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of contractile state in the intact heart.
the development of a new index of myocardial contractile function, the myocardial stiffness constant (kSM), which is independent of ventricle size.
the development of a new method for the noninvasive assessment of left ventricular contractility.

the slope of the ESPVR is a useful index of contractile state.
